title: Inner product against the noise operator as a kernel-weighted double sum
statement:
Fix a dimension $n$ and a real number $\rho$. For any two Boolean functions $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, the $L^2$ inner product of $f$ with the noised function $T_\rho g$ can be written as a double average against the noise kernel:
\[
  \langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \;=\; 2^{-n} \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n} K_\rho(x,y)\, f(x)\, g(y),
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the noise kernel and $\sigma$ is the $\pm 1$ sign encoding of a bit.
replaced:
For all $f, g : \mathrm{BoolCube}\,n \to \bbr$,
\[
  \inn{f, T_\rho g} \;=\; \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x} \sum_{y} K_\rho(x,y)\, f(x)\, g(y).
\]
